title: Public Good Provision under Locally Private Signals
summary: We study public-good provision when a planner observes agents' preferences only through a fixed local-privacy channel that randomizes each report before it reaches the planner. We characterize the optimal reduced-form allocation: the project is implemented when an aggregate posterior score is positive, where each agent's score combines the posterior expected valuation and posterior virtual value.
